content.text: No exclusivity or sole-source obligation binding Sparkling exists anywhere in the agreement. The only "exclusive" references are a non-exclusive licence grant (p0028), a non-exclusive escrow licence (p0115), a mutual exclusive-remedy provision (p0105), and non-exclusive jurisdiction (p0146) — none restricts our freedom to buy from other suppliers.

input.quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation.
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no exclusivity, sole-supplier or minimum-requirements obligation on Sparkling, which meets the preferred position (no exclusivity binding Customer). We searched the licence grant (§2), use restrictions (§3), maintenance and support (§10), fees (§11) and the general/boilerplate provisions, and ran targeted searches for "exclusive", "sole", "requirements from", "procure", "supplier", "competitor" and "third party". The only occurrences of "exclusive" are benign or favourable to us: the licence grant and the source-code escrow licence are expressly non-exclusive (p0028, p0115), §15 contains a mutual exclusive-remedy provision (p0105), and the jurisdiction clause is non-exclusive (p0146). The §3 use restrictions are ordinary software-licence limitations (copying, reverse engineering, sublicensing) and do not restrict our right to buy competing products or engage third-party maintainers. Nothing requires us to source software, maintenance or support solely from Garman, so we retain full freedom to procure from other suppliers. No redline is required.
